For each integer \(s\ge 3\), let \(D_s\) be the least positive integer \(d\) with the following property: for every collection of \(2^s-2\) Borel probability measures on \(\mathbb R^d\), each absolutely continuous with respect to \(d\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure, there exist two affine hyperplanes whose complement has exactly four connected components, each having measure \(1/4\) for every measure in the collection. The same pair of hyperplanes must work for all the measures, and no perpendicularity condition is imposed. What is the exact value of \(D_s\) as a function of \(s\)?

36	\]

43	\]

47	\]

54	\ell_u(z)=a\cdot z+b.
55	\]

63	F_{3,i}(u,v)&=\int
64	 \operatorname{sgn}\ell_u\,\operatorname{sgn}\ell_v\,d\mu_i .
65	\end{aligned}
66	\tag{2}
67	\]
68	These functions are continuous. For proper hyperplanes this follows from absolute continuity and dominated convergence; continuity at the constant signed functions follows from the same argument. They have exactly the transformation rules in the lemma.

74	 (1+\delta\operatorname{sgn}\ell_v)\,d\mu_i
75	=\frac14.
76	\tag{3}
77	\]
78	The hyperplanes must be proper and nonparallel: otherwise four signed quadrants could not all have positive measure. Their complement therefore has exactly four connected components.

83	=\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}X^{2r}Y^{2n-2-2r}.

85	\]

101	## 2. A quadratic-form construction
102	
103	The lower bound rests on the following explicit lemma.
104	
105	### Lemma
106	
107	For every even \(n\ge4\), there are \(2n-2\) real symmetric positive-definite \(n\times n\) matrices
108	\[
109	A_0,\ldots,A_{2n-3}
110	\]
111	such that
112	\[
113	u^{T}A_i v=0\quad\text{for every }i
114	\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=0\ \text{or}\ v=0.
115	\tag{6}
116	\]
117	
118	### Proof
119	
120	Write \(n=2k\), identify \(\mathbb R^n\) with \(\mathbb C^k\), and associate to \(z\in\mathbb C^k\) the polynomial
121	\[
122	P_z(t)=z_0+z_1t+\cdots+z_{k-1}t^{k-1}.
123	\]
124	
125	Choose the following \(2k-2\) distinct positive real numbers:
126	\[
127	R=\{1,2,4,6,\ldots,4k-6\}.
128	\tag{7}
129	\]
130	Their sum is odd.
131	
132	Let \(K\) be the real skew-symmetric \(k\times k\) matrix whose only nonzero entries are
133	\[
134	K_{k-2,k-1}=1,\qquad K_{k-1,k-2}=-1.
135	\]
136	Consider these \(4k-2=2n-2\) real symmetric bilinear forms:
137	\[
138	\begin{aligned}
139	B_0(z,w)&=\operatorname{Re}(z^*w),\\
140	B_1(z,w)&=\operatorname{Re}(z^*iKw),\\
141	B_{r,\mathrm{Re}}(z,w)&=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(P_z(r)P_w(r)\bigr),\\
142	B_{r,\mathrm{Im}}(z,w)&=\operatorname{Im}\bigl(P_z(r)P_w(r)\bigr),
143	\qquad r\in R.
144	\end{aligned}
145	\tag{8}
146	\]
147	They are symmetric over \(\mathbb R\); in particular \(iK\) is Hermitian.
148	
149	We claim that these forms have no common zero with \(z,w\ne0\).
150	
151	Suppose otherwise. The evaluation forms imply that \(P_zP_w\) vanishes at all \(2k-2\) points of \(R\). Its degree is at most \(2k-2\), so necessarily
152	\[
153	P_z=\alpha p_S,\qquad P_w=\beta p_T,
154	\tag{9}
155	\]
156	where \(S,T\) partition \(R\), both have size \(k-1\),
157	\[
158	p_S(t)=\prod_{r\in S}(t-r),\qquad
159	p_T(t)=\prod_{r\in T}(t-r),
160	\]
161	and \(\alpha,\beta\ne0\).
162	
163	Let \(a,b\) be the real coefficient vectors of \(p_S,p_T\), in ascending order. Because all their roots are positive, corresponding coefficients have the same alternating signs. Thus
164	\[
165	D=a^Tb>0.
166	\tag{10}
167	\]
168	Their leading coefficients are \(1\), and their next coefficients are minus their root sums. Hence
169	\[
170	\kappa=a^TKb=\sum_{r\in T}r-\sum_{r\in S}r.
171	\tag{11}
172	\]
173	This integer is odd, because the total root sum is odd. In particular, \(\kappa\ne0\).
174	
175	Now the first two forms in (8) give
176	\[
177	0=D\operatorname{Re}(\bar\alpha\beta),\qquad
178	0=-\kappa\operatorname{Im}(\bar\alpha\beta).
179	\]
180	Therefore \(\bar\alpha\beta=0\), a contradiction.
181	
182	Let \(M_0=I,M_1,\ldots,M_{2n-3}\) be the real symmetric matrices of these bilinear forms. For \(i\ge1\), put
183	\[
184	\lambda_i=1+\max_a\sum_b |(M_i)_{ab}|,\qquad
185	A_i=M_i+\lambda_i I,
186	\]
187	and put \(A_0=I\). Each \(A_i\) is positive definite, for example by strict diagonal dominance.
188	
189	If all \(u^TA_iv\) vanish, \(A_0=I\) first gives \(u^Tv=0\), after which all \(u^TM_iv\) vanish. The claim just proved establishes (6). ∎
190	
191	## 3. The lower bound: Gaussian counterexamples in dimension \(3n-3\)
192	
193	Let
194	\[
195	d_0=3n-3=(j-1)+n,
196	\]
197	and decompose
198	\[
199	\mathbb R^{d_0}=\mathbb R^{j-1}\oplus\mathbb R^n.
200	\]
201	
202	Use the \(j\) matrices from the lemma. Define \(j\) nondegenerate Gaussian probability measures with means
203	\[
204	m_0=0,\qquad m_i=(e_i,0)\quad(1\le i\le j-1)
205	\tag{12}
206	\]
207	and covariance matrices
208	\[
209	\Sigma_i=
210	\begin{pmatrix}
211	I_{j-1}&0\\
212	0&A_i
213	\end{pmatrix}.
214	\tag{13}
215	\]
216	These measures have smooth, everywhere-positive densities.
217	
218	Suppose two affine hyperplanes quarter every one of them.
219	
220	A hyperplane bisects a nondegenerate Gaussian exactly when it passes through its mean. Thus both hyperplanes must pass through every point in (12). Their offsets are zero, and their normals have the form
221	\[
222	(0,u),\qquad(0,v),\qquad u,v\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}.
223	\tag{14}
224	\]
225	
226	For the \(i\)-th Gaussian, the two defining linear functions are centered jointly Gaussian, with covariance
227	\[
228	u^TA_iv.
229	\]
230	Two centered Gaussian variables put probability \(1/4\) in every signed quadrant exactly when their covariance is zero. Indeed, if their correlation is \(\rho\),
231	\[
232	\Pr(X>0,Y>0)=\frac14+\frac{\arcsin\rho}{2\pi}.
233	\tag{15}
234	\]
235	This follows by whitening to a rotationally invariant planar Gaussian and measuring the corresponding angular sector.
236	
237	Consequently,
238	\[
239	u^TA_iv=0\qquad\text{for all }i,
240	\]
241	contradicting the lemma.
242	
243	So the required property fails in dimension \(3n-3\).
244	
245	Finally, the property is monotone upward in dimension: project measures onto a lower-dimensional coordinate space, equipartition their absolutely continuous pushforwards, and pull the hyperplanes back. Therefore failure in dimension \(3n-3\) rules out every smaller dimension as well. We have proved
246	\[
247	D_s\ge3n-2.
248	\tag{16}
249	\]
250	
251	Combining (5) and (16) proves the asserted formula.
252	
253	## 4. Exact computational checks
254	
255	The following runnable Python uses only exact integer/rational arithmetic through SymPy. It checks:
256	
257	- **every complementary root split** in the selected instances;
258	- positivity of \(a^Tb\) and the odd nonzero value of \(a^TKb\);
259	- all real quadratic-form matrices;
260	- positive definiteness of every Gaussian covariance by strict diagonal dominance;
261	- the common-bisector normal space;
262	- the entire truncated mod-\(2\) Euler polynomial.
263	
264	The general proof above handles all \(s\); these computations verify the finite certificates for \(s=3,4,5\), not merely numerical samples.
265

268	from math import comb
269	import sympy as sp
270	
271	
272	def coefficients(roots):
273	    """Coefficients of prod(t-r), ascending powers, exactly."""
274	    a = [1]
275	    for r in roots:
276	        b = [0] * (len(a) + 1)
277	        for i, x in enumerate(a):
278	            b[i] -= r * x
279	            b[i + 1] += x
280	        a = b
281	    return sp.Matrix(a)
282	
283	
284	def check(s):
285	    assert s >= 3
286	    n = 2 ** (s - 1)
287	    k = n // 2
288	    j = 2 * n - 2
289	    d0 = 3 * n - 3
290	    d = d0 + 1
291	
292	    roots = [1] + [2 * r for r in range(1, 2 * k - 2)]
293	    assert len(roots) == len(set(roots)) == 2 * k - 2
294	    assert all(r > 0 for r in roots)
295	    assert sum(roots) % 2 == 1

297	    K = sp.zeros(k)
298	    K[k - 2, k - 1] = 1
299	    K[k - 1, k - 2] = -1
300	
301	    # Exhaust all complementary root splits, modulo swapping.
302	    splits = 0
303	    for S in combinations(roots, k - 1):
304	        if 1 not in S:
305	            continue
306	        T = set(roots) - set(S)
307	        a, b = coefficients(S), coefficients(T)
308	
309	        assert a[-1] == b[-1] == 1
310	        assert all(a[i] * b[i] > 0 for i in range(k))

312	
313	        wedge = (a.T * K * b)[0]
314	        assert wedge == sum(T) - sum(S)
315	        assert wedge % 2 == 1
316	        splits += 1
317	
318	    assert splits == comb(2 * k - 2, k - 1) // 2
319	
320	    # Real coordinates are z=x+i*y.
321	    Z, I = sp.zeros(k), sp.eye(n)
322	    M = [I, sp.BlockMatrix([[Z, -K], [K, Z]]).as_explicit()]
323	
324	    for r in roots:
325	        v = sp.Matrix([r ** a for a in range(k)])
326	        V = v * v.T
327	        M += [
328	            sp.diag(V, -V),  # Re(P_z(r) P_w(r))
329	            sp.BlockMatrix([[Z, V], [V, Z]]).as_explicit()
330	        ]
331	
332	    assert len(M) == j
333	    A = [I]
334	    for B in M[1:]:
335	        assert B == B.T
336	        shift = 1 + max(
337	            sum(abs(B[a, b]) for b in range(n))
338	            for a in range(n)
339	        )
340	        C = B + shift * I
341	        assert C - shift * A[0] == B
342	        assert all(
343	            C[a, a] > sum(abs(C[a, b])
344	                          for b in range(n) if a != b)
345	            for a in range(n)
346	        )
347	        A.append(C)
348	
349	    # Exact common-bisector constraints: normal dot mean - offset = 0.
350	    means = [sp.zeros(d0, 1)]
351	    for i in range(j - 1):
352	        e = sp.zeros(d0, 1)
353	        e[i] = 1
354	        means.append(e)
355	
356	    constraints = sp.Matrix([list(mu) + [-1] for mu in means])
357	    N = constraints.nullspace()
358	    assert len(N) == n
359	    assert all(
360	        all(v[a] == 0 for a in range(j - 1)) and v[-1] == 0
361	        for v in N
362	    )
363	
364	    # Full Gaussian covariance matrices, with exact SPD certificates.
365	    for C in A:
366	        Sigma = sp.diag(sp.eye(j - 1), C)
367	        assert Sigma.shape == (d0, d0)
368	        assert Sigma[j - 1:, j - 1:] == C
369	        assert all(
370	            Sigma[a, a] > sum(abs(Sigma[a, b])
371	                              for b in range(d0) if a != b)
372	            for a in range(d0)
373	        )
374	
375	    # Entire Euler polynomial modulo (x^(d+1), y^(d+1), 2).
376	    euler = {
377	        (j + a, 2 * j - a): 1
378	        for a in range(j + 1)
379	        if j + a <= d
380	        and 2 * j - a <= d
381	        and comb(j, a) % 2
382	    }
383	    assert euler.get((3 * n - 4, 3 * n - 2)) == 1
384	
385	    print(
386	        f"s={s}: {splits} root splits certified; "
387	        f"{j} SPD covariances in dimension {d0}; "
388	        f"Euler monomials {sorted(euler)}"

397	    assert comb(2 * n - 2, n - 2) % 2 == 1
